text: Welcome to week four of the official
Arkham Menards iRacing series. In this
week, we'll be heading to the Las Vegas
Motor Speedway for 35 laps. This week in
qualifying, you'll have two choices. You
can either take it easy through lap one
and bank on a strong second lap, or you
can gun it straight out of the gate, put
a strong time on the board on lap one,
and let it all hang out on lap two. I'll
be demonstrating option two. As usual,
you want to get up to speed and get your
tires primed. If you opt to take it easy
through your first lap and build heat
more gradually, you'll be cracking the
throttle on entry as you warm up. But if
we're aiming to put up a time on both
laps, you won't want to drag your feet.
Run up against the outside wall and
build as much momentum as possible as
you take lap one. For your first flying
lap, you'll want to run full throttle on
the outside line using the steering
method from Dover. Pitch the car into
the corner, find a steering angle, and
hold it steady through the entirety of
the corner. You may need to give it more
wheel than you're comfortable with, but
if you get it right, you should be able
to hold your radius around the corner as
you run down the banking. Straighten the
wheel as the car unloads and prepare to
take on your final lap. As you watch my
second lap, you'll notice that I
completely missed my apex on both ends
of the track. This was not intentional.
I hesitated on entry and opened up my
steering for a split second in an
attempt to avoid clipping the apron. And
that just goes to show how confident you
need to be if you want to put together a
lap and find yourself on the front row.
As your final lap begins, you'll need to
arc out. Keep your eye on the white line
and crank the wheel into the corner.
Find your ideal steering angle and try
to lay your left front on the line as
you run through the corner wide open. If
you hit it just right, you should be
able to let the car track out to the
wall and exit without giving it more
wheel. Turns three and four aren't as
forgiving as one and two, so you'll
likely need to crack the throttle and
allow the car to settle on entry. Get it
down to the bottom, hug the line, and
ease back onto the throttle as you get
the car rotated through the exit. As
soon as the car settles, cut down the
track and take the shortest route to
finish your
lap. Let's take another look.

After an exhilarating qualifying
session, you'll be back to business as
usual. Starting in second gear, you want
to get out of traffic and focus on
maintaining a steady pace, running the
inside through the corners, tracking out
to the wall on the straightaways. With
this new AR car, tire temperature has
proven to be more important than tire
wear. So, you want to put yourself in a
position where you won't have to make
any drastic changes to your inputs.
While the inside will continue to be the
place to be outside of traffic, you may
find that the second and third lanes
will be viable in traffic. As the race
runs on, the inside will likely become
ingested as the difference entire wear
becomes apparent. So, if you manage
yours well, you should be able to
capitalize on those higher lanes without
much penalty. If you find yourself in
those higher lanes, you can also take
advantage of the side draft. But be
careful. Not only can net code step in
and end your race, but you may also find
that the resulting turbulence will suck
the car on the inside up the track and
potentially into you. This effect will
only be magnified as the cars tighten
up, so use the air at your own
risk. If you can pick the right battles,
make the most of your track position,
and stay out of the big packs, you might
be able to hit the jackpot this week.
Good luck.
